title: FFLAS/FFPACK WebAssembly disposition
objective: Measure and review the ten desktop-only FFLAS/FFPACK prime-matrix capabilities against existing FLINT/source-kernel WebAssembly routes; add only a bounded lazy Wasm core if representative public mul/rank/rref/nullspace workloads miss reviewed crossover targets; deliver exact native, Node-Wasm, and browser differential/route benchmarks and a precise disposition

oracles: Native public Sage.js dense GF(p) matrices using generated FFLAS/FFPACK and FLINT boundaries
Exact public matrix results and route receipts from the production Node-Wasm/browser evaluator
exceptions: A new host-neutral C/C++ core is permitted only if measurements show the source-transparent and mature FLINT Wasm closures miss representative dense-prime targets; any such core must be a bounded lazy FFLAS/FFPACK adapter, not a new matrix algorithm

handoff.summary: Reviewed all ten desktop-only FFLAS/FFPACK capabilities and rejected a new Wasm port on measured evidence. Public GF(97) and GF(65537) multiplication, rank, canonical RREF, and right nullspace use receipt-backed FLINT Wasm routes, agree exactly across native Node, Node-Wasm, and Chromium, and remain below 250 ms and 20x native through size 512. Enabled authenticated Wasm32 nmod resources for 256 <= p <= 2^32 - 1, covering the complete desktop Modular<double> range while preserving the exact portable fallback above the bound and without a resolver. Added a reproducible matched benchmark, checked-in result, detailed ten-capability disposition, and focused route/boundary regression coverage.
risks: The lane is based on 69381f47 while the integration branch advanced substantially. Repository-wide architecture and strict-baselib checks fail on unrelated stale base inventory/hyperelliptic exports; portable tests reach batch 4 before an unrelated live worktree symlink causes the native-cache safety test to fail.

The checked-in performance receipt identifies artifact sha256:4f987c63ee67c23c9dc55541dc13819d6942483c63b1f9cf705231a8a132c037 and source revision 69381f47; integration should preserve it as the reviewed measurement rather than presenting a rebuilt artifact as the measured one.
next_steps: Cherry-pick the implementation/evidence commit onto the integration branch, rebuild the production artifact, and rerun the focused test there.

Rerun architecture:check, test:portable, and test:baselib:strict on the integrated tree after the unrelated root drift and unsafe external worktree are resolved; then record fresh passing receipts and move this contract to review.

Do not add FFLAS/Givaro/BLAS to Wasm unless a future public workload outside the recorded envelope misses an explicit product budget and an end-to-end browser prototype demonstrates a win including payload and conversion costs.
